placements.title: A memory's identity is derived from what it says, not from what it was handed
placements.frame: When a submission arrives with no id of its own, what does the pipeline owe it — a name derived from its content, and a file that actually lands?
placements.why: The envelope's two expressions form one requirement context: the condition (submitted without an explicit id field) and the obligation it imposes (the pipeline must produce a slug from the memory content — via the LLM id-gen call or the deterministic slugify fallback — and commit the file successfully). This is not a one-time measurement but a standing subject: how a memory acquires an identity when none is supplied, and what counts as success in doing so. Future envelopes about id generation, slug fallbacks, or commit outcomes will keep feeding it, so it passes the grain test as a theme rather than a fact. No existing leaf exists to hold it, and nothing in the supplied structure is even close enough to warrant lineage, so it stands foundational.
